title: Send weekly digest at 09:00 in the recipient's local time
description:
The weekly digest email currently goes out at 09:00 UTC for everyone, which lands at 02:00 for our West-coast customers and 14:30 for India. Growth wants it at 09:00 in each recipient's own time zone (IANA name stored in `users.timezone`, e.g. `America/Los_Angeles`).

Add `next_digest_time(user, now_utc)` returning the next 09:00 local time strictly after `now_utc`, as an aware UTC datetime. Must be correct across daylight saving changes. Users with no time zone fall back to `UTC`.
environment: Python 3.12 (zoneinfo available). Service: notifications. Scheduler calls this function hourly.
comments: growth-pm: Open rates are 3x higher when mail arrives at start of the working day.
backend-dev: I will use zoneinfo, no pytz.
qa: Please include a DST case in the tests.
diff:
diff --git a/notifications/schedule.py b/notifications/schedule.py
--- a/notifications/schedule.py
+++ b/notifications/schedule.py
@@ -1,6 +1,28 @@
-from datetime import datetime
+from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
+from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

 DIGEST_HOUR = 9

+
+def next_digest_time(user, now_utc: datetime) -> datetime:
+    tz = ZoneInfo(user.timezone or "UTC")
+    local_now = now_utc.replace(tzinfo=tz)
+    target = local_now.replace(hour=DIGEST_HOUR, minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0)
+    if target <= local_now:
+        target += timedelta(days=1)
+    return target.astimezone(timezone.utc)
